notes:
ADMISSION IS PROVISIONAL: no measured midpoint potential for Saccharomyces cerevisiae cytochrome b5 (Cyb5p, CYB5, YNL111C, UniProt P40312) was found. Web search, PMC full text search and UniProt all come back empty; the yeast literature on CYB5 is genetic and functional (sterol C4 demethylation, azole sensitivity, P450 support), never electrochemical. This value must stay out of the default route.

WHAT IS RECORDED. The stand-in is the bovine microsomal type A cytochrome b5 tryptic fragment, +5.5 +/- 1.8 mV vs SHE, measured by mediated redox potentiometry in 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.0 (ionic strength 0.11 M), calomel reference taken as +241 mV vs SHE (Parthasarathy 2011, Table 2). The titration temperature is not stated in that paper, so T_K is null; three independent determinations on the same protein at pH 7 and 24 to 25 degrees C give +13 mV (redox potentiometry, Iyanagi 1977), +5 mV (OTTLE spectroelectrochemistry, Reid 1982) and -1.9 mV (Walker 1988). Human microsomal b5 measured by spectroelectrochemical titration at pH 7.0 and 25 degrees C is -3.2 mV (Aono 2010). Yeast Cyb5p is the type A (microsomal, ER membrane anchored) class, so the type A class statement 0 +/- 10 mV vs SHE is the right prior; the type B (outer mitochondrial membrane) proteins sit near -55 mV and are NOT the right analog.

SIGMA. sigma_kj_per_mol = 1.93 kJ/mol = n F dE with n = 2 (r_4197 transfers two electrons through two b5 molecules) and dE = 10 mV, the type A class spread. Using only the reported measurement uncertainty of 1.8 mV would give 0.35 kJ/mol, which understates the real error because the organism is wrong. Neither number covers the yeast-versus-bovine sequence difference, which is unbounded by any measurement (cytochromes b5 as a family span about 400 mV).

n_electrons is per carrier molecule (1). Reaction stoichiometry supplies the rest: r_4197 is NADH + 2 ferricytochrome b5 <=> H+ + NAD+ + 2 ferrocytochrome b5, so n = 2. With the recorded inputs, dE'0 = E'0(cyt b5) - E'0(NAD+/NADH) = 5.5 - (-320) = 325.5 mV and drG'0 = -n F dE'0 = -62.8 kJ/mol. That number is COMPUTED from the two recorded potentials, not measured, and it inherits the provisional admission.

GEM DETAIL. s_3826 Ferricytochrome b5 [m], formula Fe, charge 3; s_3827 Ferrocytochrome b5 [m], formula Fe, charge 2. gem_charge is null because the pair carries two charges. The exclusion reason in thermo_exclusions.json is no_structure_available for both. The SAME carrier class also appears in the ER membrane compartment as s_4209 Ferrocytochrome b5 [erm] and s_4210 Ferricytochrome b5 [erm] (both with empty formula, flagged pseudo_metabolite), blocking r_4196 NADH:ferricytochrome-b5 oxidoreductase and participating in r_0241 C-4 sterol methyl oxidase. The carrier potential route fixes r_4196 with exactly the same number, so the code agent should treat s_3826, s_3827, s_4209 and s_4210 as one carrier class with two oxidation states. Note the GEM's own inconsistency: the mitochondrial pair carries formula Fe with charges 3 and 2 while the ER pair carries no formula at all, and the yeast enzyme (Cyb5p) is in fact ER localized.

RHEA REPRESENTATION. Rhea models this pair as a protein-bound carrier class, not as a small molecule: RHEA:46680 (EC 1.6.2.2, the exact r_4197 chemistry) is '2 Fe(III)-[cytochrome b5] + NADH = 2 Fe(II)-[cytochrome b5] + NAD(+) + H(+)', and RHEA:62776 (the sterol C4 methyl oxidase step, r_0241) uses the same two species. Both resolve to CHEBI:29033 iron(2+) and CHEBI:29034 iron(3+) attached to the named polypeptide. This is the modeling pattern to copy: one carrier class, two oxidation states, an electron count, and a midpoint potential, with no formation energy for either state.

partner_couple_e_prime_mv.source_index is a ZERO-BASED index into sources, so 5 is the Angewandte review carrying the tabulated NAD+/NADH value of -320 mV vs SHE at pH 7, which that review attributes to Bar-Even, Flamholz, Noor and Milo (2012), the eQuilibrator group's compilation. The Thauer 1977 table the user named carries the same -320 mV, but PMC will not serve its full text as XML and its scanned PDF is behind the proof-of-work gate, so it could not be archived with a sha256. A human who wants Thauer or Alberty as the citation of record must deposit that PDF by hand.

WHAT A HUMAN STILL NEEDS TO DO. (1) Decide whether a bovine or human type A potential may stand in for yeast Cyb5p at all, or whether r_4197 and r_4196 stay unpriced. (2) If a real yeast number is wanted, it has to be measured: express the soluble heme domain of P40312 and run a mediated potentiometric titration at pH 7.0. (3) Fix the temperature: Parthasarathy 2011 does not state it, so either adopt the 24 to 25 degrees C of the three cited determinations or re-derive from Aono 2010 at 25 degrees C. (4) Deposit Reid 1982 (J Am Chem Soc 104:7516-7519) and Thauer 1977 into the mirror so the primary sources carry their own sha256 instead of being quoted secondhand.
